newsitem.title: FRANCE: US court throws out Parretti claim over MGM.
newsitem.headline: US court throws out Parretti claim over MGM.

text.p: A U.S. court has dismissed Italian financier Giancarlo Parretti's $3.9 billion suit filed against French bank Credit Lyonnais after it foreclosed on his loan to buy Hollywood studio MGM, French officials said on Tuesday.

"The Los Angeles court has thrown out Mr. Giancarlo Parretti's demands in the affair of MGM," said state-backed holding company Consortium de Realisation, which took over the bank's bad loans including the one to Parretti to buy Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer.

State-controlled Credit Lyonnais, which ran up huge losses in the early 1990s from a lending spree that went sour, was landed with MGM when Parretti defaulted on the $1.3 billion loan its former Dutch unit CLBN made to him to buy the studio.
Parretti had alleged in his suit that Credit Lyonnais acted improperly in foreclosing on the loan and conspired to take the movie studio from him.
Last month, Parretti forfeited $25,000 bail after failing to return from Italy for sentencing on a conviction of perjury and evidence tampering which carried a maximum penatly of 10 years.
Legal sources had said his failure to return to the United States meant he would lose the California lawsuit against the bank by default.
